text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- A study by Austria's defence ministry shows that fewer Austrians are prepared to defend their country. Only about 28 percent of the population would be prepared to do so. Faith in Austria's neutrality is also gradually losing ground.
- The EU commission is supporting Austria's interests in solving a transit problem with Switzerland.
- Parliamentary President Heinz Fischer said the reform of politicians' income should be ready by the summer.

- For the first time in more than two years Austria's Social Democrat Party has risen above forty percent in an opinion poll by research institute Isma. Conservatives and the far-right Freedom Party are level at 25 percent.
- Guido Schmidt-Chiari, chief executive of Creditanstalt which has only recently been sold to Bank Austria, expects Austria soon to be left without its own major business bank.
- Banks and Chamber of Economy welcome plans for supporting small companies in the export business, but see current ideas as unrealistic.
- Upper Austrian energy providers OKA and ESG plan to create a joint local telecommunications company. O-Com is planned to start operating within the year.

- Upper Austria's finance chief Christoph Leitl says the federal government should sell a 25.5 percent stake in federal grid company Verbund. Talks are being held with Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner on the provinces participating in the company.
